2) Retention / Backup carve-out proposal (draft extract below):

--- DRAFT APPENDIX X — Backup/DR Quarantine Exception ---
1. Definitions: 
   a. "DR Snapshots" means point-in-time encrypted backups created by Redwood solely for disaster recovery and operational restore processes.
   b. "Quarantine Window" means a period not to exceed ninety (90) days during which DR Snapshots containing Customer Regulated Data are retained in an isolated, access-restricted storage tier pending compliance review.
2. Exception: Redwood shall maintain DR Snapshots for a maximum of thirty (30) days under normal operations. For Customer Regulated Data where Customer provides written notice and justification, Redwood may retain DR Snapshots for an additional Quarantine Window (up to ninety (90) days) solely to permit forensic review or regulatory requests. During the Quarantine Window Redwood will: (i) limit access to named security personnel and (ii) encrypt snapshots with a separate KMS key audited in logs.
3. Scope: Exception applies only to Customer Regulated Data as identified by Customer in writing and does not permit wholesale extension of backup retention across Redwood's service.
4. Deletion: At the end of the Quarantine Window Redwood will securely delete the related DR Snapshots and retain an audit record of deletion.
---

Comments: this language aims to be narrow — customer-initiated, time-limited, and with additional access controls. Laura: can you run this by legal for any wording that might clash with our standard DR obligations?
